newsitem.title: GERMANY: Germany's summer sales period gets mixed review.
newsitem.headline: Germany's summer sales period gets mixed review.

text.p: Germany's traditional two-week summer sales period got mixed reviews from some of the country's major department stores as poor weather and worries about the economy weighed on sales in some regions.
A survey of major retailers throughout the country showed that many stores in east Germany were not happy about the number of customers as well as the level of sales.

But one official at KaDeWe in Berlin, one of the largest department stores in continental Europe, spoke of a "very, very successful" summer sales period -- one of two times a year that major sales are allowed under German law.
KaDeWe said it saw double-digit growth in sales and added it had got rid of a lot of goods to clear the way for autumn and winter items.
Many stores also said sales got a boost from longer store opening hours, which took effect earlier this year and allow stores to generally stay open until 8 p.m. on week nights.
The top store for retailer Karstadt AG in Munich said sales were "amazing" despite poor weather conditions and a late start to the summer holiday period.
Officials at the Hamburg store of Karstadt said sales were up two to three percent but its Dortmund store did not achieve year-ago sales.
Retailer Kaufhof AG, a unit of Swiss-German retailer Metro AG, also said sales at its flagship store in Cologne were satisfactory.
The Hertie department store in Dresden said it had muted sales growth as euphoria in the first few days waned.
